classifications.rationale: The Secretary must move to establish an internal FAA organization, while the Administrator determines its components and may delegate operational responsibilities; these are present organizational and management directions, not changes to external legal rights.
classifications.evidence: The Secretary of Transportation (Secretary) shall, consistent with his legal authorities, move to establish within the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) a performancebased organization

classifications.rationale: The COO is assigned an internal leadership and reporting role and must later negotiate a performance agreement; the possible bonus remains contingent on a future performance evaluation rather than being presently awarded or mandated.
classifications.evidence: The COO, in consultation with the Air Traffic Control Subcommittee of the Aviation Management Advisory Committee, shall enter into an annual performance agreement with the Administrator

classifications.rationale: The COO and ATO are directed to plan, coordinate, consult, operate, develop agreements and methods, create managerial incentives, and recommend changes; these are internal management and discretionary implementation activities without a dictated legal outcome.
classifications.evidence: The COO shall develop a 5-year strategic plan for the air traffic control system

classifications.rationale: The Air Traffic Control Subcommittee must provide ongoing internal oversight of the ATO's administration and operations, an executive-management function rather than a substantive legal consequence.
classifications.evidence: shall provide, consistent with its responsibilities under Air-21, general oversight to ATO

classifications.rationale: The Committee must submit an internal evaluative report within five years; the accompanying definition and judicial-review disclaimer do not themselves impose a substantive legal consequence or direct a later one.
classifications.evidence: shall provide to the Secretary and the Administrator a report on the operation and effectiveness of the ATO
